''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]

''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]

''Tonnaha-gusuku ato'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || [[File:Tounnahajou-Kumejima, Okinawa（登武那覇城）DSCF6529.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|26.348456|N|126.800900|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tonnaha Castle Site}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Suhara Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|スハラ城跡}}
''Suhara-jō ato'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || || {{coord|26.317084|N|126.801154|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Suhara Castle Site}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Nanatake Jinja]]
{{nihongo2|七嶽神社}}
''Nanatake Jinja'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || || {{coord|26.346874|N|126.741951|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nanatake Jinja}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Hōtoku Jinja]]
{{nihongo2|報徳神社}}
''Hōtoku Jinja'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || || {{coord|26.360222|N|126.723340|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Hōtoku Jinja}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Kubaka Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|クバカ城跡}}
''Kubaka-jō ato'' || [[Miyakojima|Miyakojima Island]] || [[Miyakojima, Okinawa|Miyakojima]] || || [[File:Kubaka Castle Gate.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.730925|N|125.300026|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kubaka Castle Site}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Tarama Jinja]]
{{nihongo2|多良間神社}}
''Tarama Jinja'' || [[Tarama Island]] || [[Tarama, Okinawa|Tarama]] || || || {{coord|24.670737|N|124.700142|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tarama Jinja}} || || |- |} ==Registered Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, two Monuments have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan#categories of registered Cultural Properties|registered]] (as opposed to [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]]) as Historic Sites at a national level.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:登録文化財 |trans-title=Number of Registered Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 登録記念物 (遺跡関係 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Okinawa Prefectural Railways]] [[Yonabaru Station]] Site
{{nihongo2|沖縄県鉄道[[:ja:与那原駅|与那原駅]]跡}}
''Okinawa-ken tetsudō Yonabaru-eki ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Yonabaru, Okinawa|Yonabaru]] || || [[File:Yonabaru Station of Okinawa Prefectural Railways.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.19958|N|127.75480|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Okinawa Prefectural Railways Yonabaru Station Site}} || || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/411/00004009 ] |- | align="center"|[[Heshikiya Sugar Refining Site]]
{{nihongo2|平敷屋製糖工場跡}}
''Heshikiya seitō kōjō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || || || {{coord|26.37929|N|127.85730|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Heshikiya Sugar Refining Site}} || || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/411/00003916 ] |- |} {{Complete list|date=October 2024}} {{Historic Sites of Japan}} {{Cultural Properties of Japan - {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]
{{nihongo2|フルスト原遺跡}}
''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|安慶名城跡}}
''Agena-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[gusuku]] fortified in the fifteenth century{{cite web |url=http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |script-title=ja:見どころ：国指定の文化財 |trans-title=Sightseeing Places - Nationally designated Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502005624/http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |archivedate=2 May 2012 }} || [[File:Agenagusuku.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.38088963|N|127.85036561|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Agena Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3020 ] |- | align="center"|[[Iha Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|伊波貝塚}}
''Iha kaizuka'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site discovered in 1920; finds include shells, fish bones, animal borns, earthenware, stoneware, and goods made of horn{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=139844 |script-title=ja:伊波貝塚 |trans-title=Iha Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || [[File:Iha Shell Mound.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.42047542|N|127.82081653|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Iha Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3018 ] |- | align="center"|[[Ireibaru]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:伊礼原遺跡|伊礼原遺跡]]}}
''Ireibaru iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Chatan, Okinawa|Chatan]] || early [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site; goods of [[jade]] and [[obsidian]] are evidence of early maritime trade || || {{coord|26.32434512|N|127.7586994|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ireibaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003665 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uegusuku Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|宇江城城跡}}
''Uegusuku-jō ato'' || [[Kumejima|Kumejima Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || of uncertain date, but probably razed at the time of assimilation into the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] c.1500; finds include Chinese ceramics and fish bones; the view extends over the entire island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140627 |script-title=ja:宇江城城跡 |trans-title=Uegusuku Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.37696201|N|126.77013595|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uegusuku Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003648 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uzahama Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:宇佐浜遺跡|宇佐浜遺跡]]}}
''Uzahama iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Kunigami, Okinawa|Kunigami]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi]] site on the northern tip of the island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |script-title=ja:宇佐浜遺跡 |trans-title=Uzahama Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120708014450/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |archivedate=8 July 2012 }} || || {{coord|26.86602391|N|128.26020475|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uzahama Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3016 ] |- | align="center"|[[Urasoe Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|浦添城跡}}
''Urazoe-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Urasoe, Okinawa|Urasoe]] || fortifications date back to C13/C14; incurred heavy damage during the Battle of Okinawa{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=206923 |script-title=ja:浦添城跡 |trans-title=Urazoe Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || [[File:Urasoe Castle Walls.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.24648788|N|127.73227642|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Urazoe Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3067 ] |- | align="center"|[[Enkaku-ji (Okinawa)|Enkaku-ji]] Site
{{nihongo2|円覚寺跡}}
''Enkaku-ji ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Naha, Okinawa|Naha]] || founded in 1492 by [[Shō Shin]]; the wooden temple buildings were destroyed during the war, an ornately carved stone bridge ([[List of Important Cultural Properties of Japan (Okinawa: structures)|ICP]]) survives{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=196300 |script-title=ja:旧円覚寺放生橋 |trans-title=Engaku-ji Hōjō Bridge |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || [[File:Enkaku-ji(Shuri)200703.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.21832884|N|127.71963726|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Enkakuji Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|3]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3026 ] |- | align="center"|[[Ogidō Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:荻堂貝塚|荻堂貝塚]]}}
''Ogidō kaizuka'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Kitanakagusuku, Okinawa|Kitanakagusuku]] || [[Jōmon period]], with a 1.2 m thick deposit of shells{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=162738 |script-title=ja:荻堂貝塚 |trans-title=Ogidō Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.29323453|N|127.79865309|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ogidō Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3022 ] |- | align="center"|[[Shimotabaru Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:下田原城|下田原城]]跡}}
''Shimotabaru-jō ato'' || [[Hateruma|Hateruma Island]] || [[Taketomi, Okinawa|Taketomi]] || || [[File:2016-02-26 Shimotabaru-jou,Hateruma 下田原城・ぶりぶち公園 波照間島 DSCF2525.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|24.06934384|N|123.77915508|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Shimotabaru Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3366 ] |- | align="center"|[[Tamagusuku Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|玉城城跡}}
''Tamagusuku-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Nanjō, Okinawa|Nanjō]] || || [[File:Tamagusuku arch.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.1441253|N|127.78067218|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tamagusuku Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3066 ] |- | align="center"|[[Tamaudun]]
{{nihongo2|玉陵}}
''Tamaudun'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Naha, Okinawa|Naha]] || royal mausoleum complex constructed in 1501; [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu|World Heritage Site]] || [[File:Tamaudun03bs3200.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.21831078|N|127.71465507|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tamaudūn}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|7]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3027 ] |- | align="center"|[[Kushibaru Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|具志原貝塚}}
''Kushibaru kaizuka'' || [[Iejima|Ie Island]] || [[Ie, Okinawa|Ie]] || variety of shells and [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] and [[Yayoi period|Yayoi]] earthenware{{cite web |url=http://www.iejima.org/ieson/index.php?oid=42&dtype=1000&pid=100 |script-title=ja:具志原貝塚 |trans-title=Kushibaru Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ie, Okinawa|Ie Village]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.7083557|N|127.80085456|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kushibaru Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3063 ] |- | align="center"|[[Gushikawa Castle (Itoman)|Gushikawa Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|具志川城跡}}
''Gushikawa-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Itoman, Okinawa|Itoman]] || C13-C15 Chinese ceramics found during excavations; thirteen-year restoration project between 2000 and 2012{{cite web |url=http://www.city.itoman.okinawa.jp/kyouiku_bunka/bunkazai/old/gushikawajyouseki/gusikawajyosekihozonjigyo.htm |script-title=ja:具志川城跡保存修理事業 |trans-title=Restoration of Gushikawa Castle |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Itoman, Okinawa|Itoman City]] |accessdate=31 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120729141700/http://www.city.itoman.okinawa.jp/kyouiku_bunka/bunkazai/old/gushikawajyouseki/gusikawajyosekihozonjigyo.htm |archivedate=29 July 2012 }} || [[File:Historic sites of Gushikawa Castle 01 at Itoman city.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|26.08027649|N|127.66431713|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Gushikawa Castle Site (Itoman)}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3032 ] |- | align="center"|[[Gushikawa Castle (Kume)|Gushikawa Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|具志川城跡}}
''Gushikawa-jō ato'' || [[Kumejima Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || same name but distinct from the castle in Itoman || || {{coord|26.38470951|N|126.75190674|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Gushikawa Castle (Kumejima)}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3057 ] |- | align="center"|[[Kunigami Hōsei Kaidō]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:国頭方西海道|国頭方西海道]]}}
''Kunigami hōsei kaidō'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Onna, Okinawa|Onna]] || historic route on the west coast of the island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=207233 |script-title=ja:国頭方西海道 |trans-title=Kunigami Hōsei Kaidō |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.43476258|N|127.78981966|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kunigamihōseikaidō}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3412 ] |- | align="center"|[[Nakijin Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|今帰仁城跡 附シイナ城跡}}

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]
{{nihongo2|フルスト原遺跡}}
''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|安慶名城跡}}
''Agena-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[gusuku]] fortified in the fifteenth century{{cite web |url=http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |script-title=ja:見どころ：国指定の文化財 |trans-title=Sightseeing Places - Nationally designated Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502005624/http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |archivedate=2 May 2012 }} || [[File:Agenagusuku.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.38088963|N|127.85036561|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Agena Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3020 ] |- | align="center"|[[Iha Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|伊波貝塚}}
''Iha kaizuka'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site discovered in 1920; finds include shells, fish bones, animal borns, earthenware, stoneware, and goods made of horn{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=139844 |script-title=ja:伊波貝塚 |trans-title=Iha Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || [[File:Iha Shell Mound.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.42047542|N|127.82081653|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Iha Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3018 ] |- | align="center"|[[Ireibaru]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:伊礼原遺跡|伊礼原遺跡]]}}
''Ireibaru iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Chatan, Okinawa|Chatan]] || early [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site; goods of [[jade]] and [[obsidian]] are evidence of early maritime trade || || {{coord|26.32434512|N|127.7586994|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ireibaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003665 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uegusuku Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|宇江城城跡}}
''Uegusuku-jō ato'' || [[Kumejima|Kumejima Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || of uncertain date, but probably razed at the time of assimilation into the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] c.1500; finds include Chinese ceramics and fish bones; the view extends over the entire island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140627 |script-title=ja:宇江城城跡 |trans-title=Uegusuku Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.37696201|N|126.77013595|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uegusuku Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003648 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uzahama Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:宇佐浜遺跡|宇佐浜遺跡]]}}
''Uzahama iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Kunigami, Okinawa|Kunigami]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi]] site on the northern tip of the island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |script-title=ja:宇佐浜遺跡 |trans-title=Uzahama Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120708014450/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |archivedate=8 July 2012 }} || || {{coord|26.86602391|N|128.26020475|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uzahama Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3016 ] |- | align="center"|[[Urasoe Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|浦添城跡}}
''Urazoe-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Urasoe, Okinawa|Urasoe]] || fortifications date back to C13/C14; incurred heavy damage during the Battle of Okinawa{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=206923 |script-title=ja:浦添城跡 |trans-title=Urazoe Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || [[File:Urasoe Castle Walls.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.24648788|N|127.73227642|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Urazoe Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3067 ] |- | align="center"|[[Enkaku-ji (Okinawa)|Enkaku-ji]] Site
{{nihongo2|円覚寺跡}}

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]

''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]

''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]

''Tonnaha-gusuku ato'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || [[File:Tounnahajou-Kumejima, Okinawa（登武那覇城）DSCF6529.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|26.348456|N|126.800900|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tonnaha Castle Site}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Suhara Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|スハラ城跡}}
''Suhara-jō ato'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || || {{coord|26.317084|N|126.801154|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Suhara Castle Site}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Nanatake Jinja]]
{{nihongo2|七嶽神社}}
''Nanatake Jinja'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || || {{coord|26.346874|N|126.741951|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nanatake Jinja}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Hōtoku Jinja]]
{{nihongo2|報徳神社}}
''Hōtoku Jinja'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || || {{coord|26.360222|N|126.723340|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Hōtoku Jinja}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Kubaka Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|クバカ城跡}}
''Kubaka-jō ato'' || [[Miyakojima|Miyakojima Island]] || [[Miyakojima, Okinawa|Miyakojima]] || || [[File:Kubaka Castle Gate.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.730925|N|125.300026|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kubaka Castle Site}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Tarama Jinja]]
{{nihongo2|多良間神社}}
''Tarama Jinja'' || [[Tarama Island]] || [[Tarama, Okinawa|Tarama]] || || || {{coord|24.670737|N|124.700142|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tarama Jinja}} || || |- |} ==Registered Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, two Monuments have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan#categories of registered Cultural Properties|registered]] (as opposed to [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]]) as Historic Sites at a national level.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:登録文化財 |trans-title=Number of Registered Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 登録記念物 (遺跡関係 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Okinawa Prefectural Railways]] [[Yonabaru Station]] Site
{{nihongo2|沖縄県鉄道[[:ja:与那原駅|与那原駅]]跡}}
''Okinawa-ken tetsudō Yonabaru-eki ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Yonabaru, Okinawa|Yonabaru]] || || [[File:Yonabaru Station of Okinawa Prefectural Railways.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.19958|N|127.75480|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Okinawa Prefectural Railways Yonabaru Station Site}} || || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/411/00004009 ] |- | align="center"|[[Heshikiya Sugar Refining Site]]
{{nihongo2|平敷屋製糖工場跡}}
''Heshikiya seitō kōjō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || || || {{coord|26.37929|N|127.85730|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Heshikiya Sugar Refining Site}} || || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/411/00003916 ] |- |} {{Complete list|date=October 2024}} {{Historic Sites of Japan}} {{Cultural Properties of Japan - {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]
{{nihongo2|フルスト原遺跡}}
''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|安慶名城跡}}
''Agena-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[gusuku]] fortified in the fifteenth century{{cite web |url=http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |script-title=ja:見どころ：国指定の文化財 |trans-title=Sightseeing Places - Nationally designated Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502005624/http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |archivedate=2 May 2012 }} || [[File:Agenagusuku.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.38088963|N|127.85036561|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Agena Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3020 ] |- | align="center"|[[Iha Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|伊波貝塚}}
''Iha kaizuka'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site discovered in 1920; finds include shells, fish bones, animal borns, earthenware, stoneware, and goods made of horn{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=139844 |script-title=ja:伊波貝塚 |trans-title=Iha Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || [[File:Iha Shell Mound.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.42047542|N|127.82081653|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Iha Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3018 ] |- | align="center"|[[Ireibaru]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:伊礼原遺跡|伊礼原遺跡]]}}
''Ireibaru iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Chatan, Okinawa|Chatan]] || early [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site; goods of [[jade]] and [[obsidian]] are evidence of early maritime trade || || {{coord|26.32434512|N|127.7586994|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ireibaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003665 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uegusuku Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|宇江城城跡}}
''Uegusuku-jō ato'' || [[Kumejima|Kumejima Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || of uncertain date, but probably razed at the time of assimilation into the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] c.1500; finds include Chinese ceramics and fish bones; the view extends over the entire island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140627 |script-title=ja:宇江城城跡 |trans-title=Uegusuku Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.37696201|N|126.77013595|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uegusuku Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003648 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uzahama Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:宇佐浜遺跡|宇佐浜遺跡]]}}
''Uzahama iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Kunigami, Okinawa|Kunigami]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi]] site on the northern tip of the island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |script-title=ja:宇佐浜遺跡 |trans-title=Uzahama Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120708014450/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |archivedate=8 July 2012 }} || || {{coord|26.86602391|N|128.26020475|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uzahama Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3016 ] |- | align="center"|[[Urasoe Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|浦添城跡}}
''Urazoe-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Urasoe, Okinawa|Urasoe]] || fortifications date back to C13/C14; incurred heavy damage during the Battle of Okinawa{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=206923 |script-title=ja:浦添城跡 |trans-title=Urazoe Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || [[File:Urasoe Castle Walls.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.24648788|N|127.73227642|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Urazoe Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3067 ] |- | align="center"|[[Enkaku-ji (Okinawa)|Enkaku-ji]] Site
{{nihongo2|円覚寺跡}}
''Enkaku-ji ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Naha, Okinawa|Naha]] || founded in 1492 by [[Shō Shin]]; the wooden temple buildings were destroyed during the war, an ornately carved stone bridge ([[List of Important Cultural Properties of Japan (Okinawa: structures)|ICP]]) survives{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=196300 |script-title=ja:旧円覚寺放生橋 |trans-title=Engaku-ji Hōjō Bridge |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || [[File:Enkaku-ji(Shuri)200703.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.21832884|N|127.71963726|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Enkakuji Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|3]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3026 ] |- | align="center"|[[Ogidō Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:荻堂貝塚|荻堂貝塚]]}}
''Ogidō kaizuka'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Kitanakagusuku, Okinawa|Kitanakagusuku]] || [[Jōmon period]], with a 1.2 m thick deposit of shells{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=162738 |script-title=ja:荻堂貝塚 |trans-title=Ogidō Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.29323453|N|127.79865309|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ogidō Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3022 ] |- | align="center"|[[Shimotabaru Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:下田原城|下田原城]]跡}}
''Shimotabaru-jō ato'' || [[Hateruma|Hateruma Island]] || [[Taketomi, Okinawa|Taketomi]] || || [[File:2016-02-26 Shimotabaru-jou,Hateruma 下田原城・ぶりぶち公園 波照間島 DSCF2525.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|24.06934384|N|123.77915508|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Shimotabaru Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3366 ] |- | align="center"|[[Tamagusuku Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|玉城城跡}}
''Tamagusuku-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Nanjō, Okinawa|Nanjō]] || || [[File:Tamagusuku arch.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.1441253|N|127.78067218|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tamagusuku Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3066 ] |- | align="center"|[[Tamaudun]]
{{nihongo2|玉陵}}
''Tamaudun'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Naha, Okinawa|Naha]] || royal mausoleum complex constructed in 1501; [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu|World Heritage Site]] || [[File:Tamaudun03bs3200.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.21831078|N|127.71465507|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tamaudūn}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|7]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3027 ] |- | align="center"|[[Kushibaru Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|具志原貝塚}}
''Kushibaru kaizuka'' || [[Iejima|Ie Island]] || [[Ie, Okinawa|Ie]] || variety of shells and [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] and [[Yayoi period|Yayoi]] earthenware{{cite web |url=http://www.iejima.org/ieson/index.php?oid=42&dtype=1000&pid=100 |script-title=ja:具志原貝塚 |trans-title=Kushibaru Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ie, Okinawa|Ie Village]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.7083557|N|127.80085456|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kushibaru Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3063 ] |- | align="center"|[[Gushikawa Castle (Itoman)|Gushikawa Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|具志川城跡}}
''Gushikawa-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Itoman, Okinawa|Itoman]] || C13-C15 Chinese ceramics found during excavations; thirteen-year restoration project between 2000 and 2012{{cite web |url=http://www.city.itoman.okinawa.jp/kyouiku_bunka/bunkazai/old/gushikawajyouseki/gusikawajyosekihozonjigyo.htm |script-title=ja:具志川城跡保存修理事業 |trans-title=Restoration of Gushikawa Castle |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Itoman, Okinawa|Itoman City]] |accessdate=31 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120729141700/http://www.city.itoman.okinawa.jp/kyouiku_bunka/bunkazai/old/gushikawajyouseki/gusikawajyosekihozonjigyo.htm |archivedate=29 July 2012 }} || [[File:Historic sites of Gushikawa Castle 01 at Itoman city.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|26.08027649|N|127.66431713|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Gushikawa Castle Site (Itoman)}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3032 ] |- | align="center"|[[Gushikawa Castle (Kume)|Gushikawa Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|具志川城跡}}
''Gushikawa-jō ato'' || [[Kumejima Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || same name but distinct from the castle in Itoman || || {{coord|26.38470951|N|126.75190674|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Gushikawa Castle (Kumejima)}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3057 ] |- | align="center"|[[Kunigami Hōsei Kaidō]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:国頭方西海道|国頭方西海道]]}}
''Kunigami hōsei kaidō'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Onna, Okinawa|Onna]] || historic route on the west coast of the island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=207233 |script-title=ja:国頭方西海道 |trans-title=Kunigami Hōsei Kaidō |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.43476258|N|127.78981966|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kunigamihōseikaidō}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3412 ] |- | align="center"|[[Nakijin Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|今帰仁城跡 附シイナ城跡}}

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]
{{nihongo2|フルスト原遺跡}}
''Furusutobaru iseki'' || [[Ishigaki Island]] || [[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki]] || C13-C15 [[gusuku]]-style fortifications, domestic buildings, [[utaki]], and tombs extending for 12.3 ha on the {{nihongo|Ryūkyū limestone|[[:ja:琉球石灰岩|琉球石灰岩]]}} hills overlooking Miyara Bay; said to have been used by [[Oyake Akahachi]] and suppressed by the forces of [[Shō Shin]] in 1500; finds include local pottery, white porcelain and [[celadon]] from China, and the bones of horses and cows{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.okinawa.jp/shin-ishigaki/yougo/furusuto.html |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡 |trans-title=Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |script-title=ja:フルスト原遺跡の概要 |trans-title=Overview of the Furusutobaru Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Ishigaki, Okinawa|Ishigaki City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070502130351/http://www.city.ishigaki.okinawa.jp/400000/410000/410400/bunkaka/furusutobaru.htm |archivedate=2 May 2007 }} || [[File:Ishigaki furusutobaru iseki.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.3511203|N|124.19500445|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Furusutobaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3059 ] |- | align="center"|[[Agena Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|安慶名城跡}}
''Agena-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[gusuku]] fortified in the fifteenth century{{cite web |url=http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |script-title=ja:見どころ：国指定の文化財 |trans-title=Sightseeing Places - Nationally designated Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma City]] |accessdate=30 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502005624/http://www.city.uruma.lg.jp/1/209.html |archivedate=2 May 2012 }} || [[File:Agenagusuku.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.38088963|N|127.85036561|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Agena Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3020 ] |- | align="center"|[[Iha Shell Mound]]
{{nihongo2|伊波貝塚}}
''Iha kaizuka'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Uruma, Okinawa|Uruma]] || [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site discovered in 1920; finds include shells, fish bones, animal borns, earthenware, stoneware, and goods made of horn{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=139844 |script-title=ja:伊波貝塚 |trans-title=Iha Shell Mound |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || [[File:Iha Shell Mound.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.42047542|N|127.82081653|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Iha Shell Mound}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3018 ] |- | align="center"|[[Ireibaru]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:伊礼原遺跡|伊礼原遺跡]]}}
''Ireibaru iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Chatan, Okinawa|Chatan]] || early [[Jōmon period|Jōmon]] site; goods of [[jade]] and [[obsidian]] are evidence of early maritime trade || || {{coord|26.32434512|N|127.7586994|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ireibaru Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003665 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uegusuku Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|宇江城城跡}}
''Uegusuku-jō ato'' || [[Kumejima|Kumejima Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || of uncertain date, but probably razed at the time of assimilation into the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] c.1500; finds include Chinese ceramics and fish bones; the view extends over the entire island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140627 |script-title=ja:宇江城城跡 |trans-title=Uegusuku Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=30 May 2012}} || || {{coord|26.37696201|N|126.77013595|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uegusuku Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003648 ] |- | align="center"|[[Uzahama Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:宇佐浜遺跡|宇佐浜遺跡]]}}
''Uzahama iseki'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Kunigami, Okinawa|Kunigami]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi]] site on the northern tip of the island{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |script-title=ja:宇佐浜遺跡 |trans-title=Uzahama Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120708014450/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192272 |archivedate=8 July 2012 }} || || {{coord|26.86602391|N|128.26020475|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Uzahama Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3016 ] |- | align="center"|[[Urasoe Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|浦添城跡}}
''Urazoe-jō ato'' || [[Okinawa Island]] || [[Urasoe, Okinawa|Urasoe]] || fortifications date back to C13/C14; incurred heavy damage during the Battle of Okinawa{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=206923 |script-title=ja:浦添城跡 |trans-title=Urazoe Castle Site |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 May 2012}} || [[File:Urasoe Castle Walls.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|26.24648788|N|127.73227642|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Urazoe Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3067 ] |- | align="center"|[[Enkaku-ji (Okinawa)|Enkaku-ji]] Site
{{nihongo2|円覚寺跡}}

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]]'''.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} Much of the heritage of the [[Ryūkyū Kingdom]] and [[Ryukyu Islands|Islands]] was destroyed during the [[Battle of Okinawa]]. The mausoleum complex of [[Tamaudun]], [[Shuri Castle]], [[Katsuren Castle]], [[Nakagusuku Castle]], [[Nakijin Castle]], [[Zakimi Castle]], [[Sefa-utaki]], and [[Sonohyan-utaki]] all form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site [[Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/972/ |title=Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |accessdate=24 September 2017}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, forty-three Sites have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pref.okinawa.jp/kyoiku/edu/1008462/1008471/1028479.html |script-title=ja:国・県・市町村指定文化財 |trans-title=National, Prefectural, and Municipal Cultural Properties |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Okinawa Prefecture]] |date=1 May 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Furusutobaru Castle]]

''Hōtoku Jinja'' || [[Kume Island]] || [[Kumejima, Okinawa|Kumejima]] || || || {{coord|26.360222|N|126.723340|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Hōtoku Jinja}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Kubaka Castle]] Site
{{nihongo2|クバカ城跡}}
''Kubaka-jō ato'' || [[Miyakojima|Miyakojima Island]] || [[Miyakojima, Okinawa|Miyakojima]] || || [[File:Kubaka Castle Gate.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|24.730925|N|125.300026|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kubaka Castle Site}} || || |- | align="center"|[[Tarama Jinja]]
{{nihongo2|多良間神社}}
''Tarama Jinja'' || [[Tarama Island]] || [[Tarama, Okinawa|Tarama]] || || || {{coord|24.670737|N|124.700142|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tarama Jinja}} || || |- |} ==Registered Historic Sites== As of 1 October 2024, two Monuments have been [[Cultural Properties of Japan#categories of registered Cultural Properties|registered]] (as opposed to [[Cultural Properties of Japan|designated]]) as Historic Sites at a national level.{{cite web |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:登録文化財 |trans-title=Number of Registered Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=24 October 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 登録記念物 (遺跡関係 沖縄県) |language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=24 October 2024}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="20%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Island !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|[[Okinawa Prefectural Railways]] [[Yonabaru Station]] Site
